title: Straitbridge POC workshop and success criteria
content:
Objective:
Short: Rapidly validate that Redwood can serve Straitbridge’s real-time summarization pipeline within their latency, privacy, and cost constraints for a 6-week pilot.

Problem statement / customer need:
Straitbridge (financial research platform) needs a low-latency, private inference path for ingesting user documents, running chunked summarization + entity-redaction, and surfacing near-instant previews in the UI. They must meet regulatory data handling rules (no customer data leaving VPC) and keep incremental cost below $0.02 per summary during the pilot.

Scope (what we will and will not do in this POC):
- In scope:
  - Deploy Redwood Private in Straitbridge sandbox VPC (single cluster, non-prod).
  - Host a trimmed model variant (quantized) selected from Redwood catalog that supports summarization.
  - Implement a KV-cache prefix strategy for repeated doc updates.
  - Measure latency/throughput, cost per summary, and quality on a 1000-item eval set.
  - Workshop with their SREs on routing/fallback policies and basic rollout.
- Out of scope:
  - Long-term autoscaling policies for production traffic shaping.
  - Integrations with their billing system.
  - Full on-prem air-gapped deployment (pilot uses VPC-peered managed control plane).

Success criteria (must be met for POC to be considered successful):
1) Latency and performance
  - Median end-to-end (request -> final token) latency <= 300ms for 256-token inputs on the test harness (95th <= 550ms).
  - Sustained throughput of 120 summaries/min on single reserved node under representative workload (concurrency mix documented).
2) Cost
  - Effective incremental cost <= $0.02 per summary when batching and KV cache active (measured on Redwood billing estimate).
3) Quality and correctness
  - Rouge-L on the 1,000-item eval set >= baseline_model_score - 3 points (baseline provided by Straitbridge).
  - Entity redaction precision >= 95% (sampled manual review of 200 items).
4) Security and compliance
  - All PII and documents stay in their VPC (no egress to public internet).
  - KMS key integration validated for encryption-at-rest.
5) Operability
  - Console dashboards show per-route cost and latency; at least two alerting rules configured (latency p95 > threshold, error rate > 1%).
  - On-call handoff documented and initial playbook for fallback model configured.
6) Customer sign-off criteria
  - Straitbridge SRE and Product Manager approve final demo and the post-pilot runbook (explicit sign-off doc).

Technical acceptance tests (concrete checks we will run):
- E2E test harness that simulates UI flow with 256 token average inputs and measures latency distribution.
- Batch effect test: run same 1,000-item set with and without caching/batching, capture cost delta.
- Stress test: ramp to 3x target concurrency for 10 minutes and verify graceful degradation (fallback model + queueing) without dropped requests > 1%.
- Security test: validate network egress and KMS usage via customer-side audit logs.

Workshop agenda (Week 0 kickoff, 90m remote):
- 00-10m: Introductions + intended outcomes (SE, SRE, Product).
- 10-25m: Customer architecture walkthrough (Straitbridge engineer).
- 25-45m: Redwood design proposal (runtime sizing, model variant, caching plan).
- 45-60m: Deployment runbook & required credentials checklist.
- 60-80m: Success criteria review & acceptance tests.
- 80-90m: Action items, owners, and scheduling the onboarding week.

Deployment plan (high level):
1) Prep (Week 0): credentials exchange, network peering, KMS policy review, NFS/S3 access plan.
2) Infra deploy (Week 1): bootstrap control plane in their sandbox VPC + single worker pool, deploy model artifact.
3) Integration (Week 2): wire test harness, implement redaction preprocessor in a sidecar, enable prefix cache.
4) Measurement (Week 3): run eval set, collect metrics, iterate on batch size/quantization.
5) Adoption demo (Week 4): demo to stakeholders, finalize runbook, collect sign-offs.

Roles and owners (initial):
- Redwood SE lead: Maya Chen (overall SE contact, kickoff lead).
- Redwood infra support: Raj Patel (cluster bootstrap, control plane).
- Redwood Optimize advisor: Sofia Martinez (batch/cache tuning).
- Customer SRE: Devon Lee (Straitbridge).
- Customer Product: Anika Rao (Straitbridge PM).

Open questions / risks (to resolve in workshop):
- Which model variant will they accept for a private deployment (legal/regulatory constraints vs. quality)?
- Does their SOC require additional logging redaction before logs leave nodes?
- Network egress: can we use shared VPC peering or must we set up privateLink?
- Cost model variance if traffic pattern changes (spiky usage may invalidate $/summary estimate).

Artifacts to collect from customer before Week 1:
- Sandbox VPC CIDR and peering details.
- KMS key ARN and minimum access policy.
- Sample dataset (anonymized) of 1,200 documents for eval (or synthetic equivalent).
- Contact for firewall rules and an SRE escalation contact.

Action items (first pass):
- [Maya] Draft deployment runbook template and share by 2025-02-14.
- [Raj] Prepare Terraform snippet for control plane peering by 2025-02-18.
- [Sofia] Create initial batching profile and recommended quantization by 2025-02-20.
- [Devon] Provide sandbox VPC details and sample dataset by 2025-02-17.

Notes to self / SE playbook fragments:
- Try batch size 8 with prefix cache TTL=10s as starting point; monitor p95 latency for tokens beyond 128.
- If 95th latency > target, consider switching to half-precision variant or enabling KV cache prefetch.
- Keep a small canary route that always uses baseline model (for quick quality regressions).

Next meeting: follow-up workshop to confirm infra details scheduled for 2025-02-18 10:00 PST (invite pending).

Appendix: quick evaluation matrix (for internal use)
- Metric: median latency | target: <=300ms | measurement: E2E harness
- Metric: cost/summary | target: <=$0.02 | measurement: Redwood billing sim + observed usage
- Metric: rouge-L vs baseline | target: within -3 pts | measurement: automated eval suite
- Metric: redaction precision | target: >=95% | measurement: manual review sample of 200

End of doc.
